**12.3 Project Kickoff**

A project kickoff is the formal start of the work. The lead is responsible for arranging the kickoff meeting and for making sure the following are in place beforehand:

- A one-page project brief, saved to the shared drive under Projects / [Project Name] / Brief.
- A named deputy (see 12.2).
- A provisional budget, agreed with Helen.
- A list of milestones, even if the dates are rough.

The kickoff meeting should cover the project brief, the milestones, and the communication plan (how often the team will meet, where notes are stored, and who updates the status notes).

**12.4 Project Milestones**

Standard milestones are used across all projects. They are not compulsory for very small pieces of work, but for anything expected to last more than a month, the lead should use them:

- **M1 – Kickoff**: Project brief agreed, team confirmed, budget signed off.
- **M2 – Discovery**: Requirements gathered, current processes reviewed, gaps identified.
- **M3 – Design**: Proposed approach written up, costs confirmed, go/no-go decision.
- **M4 – Build**: Work carried out, testing done, training material prepared.
- **M5 – Go Live**: New process or tool in use, old process retired.
- **M6 – Review**: Project closed, lessons learned logged, final budget checked.

Milestones are recorded in the Project Status Notes with a target date and an actual date. If a milestone slips by more than two weeks, the lead must tell Helen and update the status notes the same day.

**12.5 Project Status Notes**

The Project Status Notes file is the single source of truth for project progress. It is a spreadsheet on the shared drive, with one tab per project. Each tab has columns for:

- Milestone number and name
- Target date (ISO format, YYYY-MM-DD)
- Actual date (left blank until the milestone is reached)
- Owner
- Notes (brief, no more than a couple of sentences)

The lead (or the deputy, if the lead is away) updates the status notes every Friday by 4pm. If there is nothing to update, the lead writes "No change" in the notes column for the most recent milestone rather than leaving it blank. This helps us see at a glance which projects are moving and which have stalled.

**12.6 Project Status Meetings**

We hold a project status meeting on the first Monday of each month, 10:00–11:00, in the meeting room on the first floor. The meeting is chaired by Helen. Each project lead gives a five-minute update covering:

- What has been completed since the last meeting.
- What is planned for the next month.
- Any risks or blockers, and who is helping to resolve them.

Notes from the meeting are taken by Amelia and circulated within two working days. Action items from the meeting are added to the Action Register (see section 13).

**12.7 Project Closures**

When a project reaches M6 and is ready to close, the lead must:

1. Confirm all milestones are marked complete in the status notes.
2. Log the lessons learned in the Lessons Learned file (one page maximum).
3. Confirm the final budget with Helen and flag any overspend.
4. Move the project folder on the shared drive to Projects / Closed / [Year] / [Project Name].

Once a project is closed, the Xero project code is archived. Do not reuse a closed project code for new work – ask Amelia if you need a new code.

**12.3 Project Kickoff**

A project kickoff is the formal start of the work. The lead is responsible for arranging the kickoff meeting and for making sure the following are in place beforehand:

- A one-page project brief, saved to the shared drive under Projects / [Project Name] / Brief.
- A named deputy (see 12.2).
- A provisional budget, agreed with Helen.
- A list of milestones, even if the dates are rough.

The kickoff meeting should cover the project brief, the milestones, and the communication plan (how often the team will meet, where notes are stored, and who updates the status notes).

**12.4 Project Milestones**

Standard milestones are used across all projects. They are not compulsory for very small pieces of work, but for anything expected to last more than a month, the lead should use them:

- **M1 – Kickoff**: Project brief agreed, team confirmed, budget signed off.
- **M2 – Discovery**: Requirements gathered, current processes reviewed, gaps identified.
- **M3 – Design**: Proposed approach written up, costs confirmed, go/no-go decision.
- **M4 – Build**: Work carried out, testing done, training material prepared.
- **M5 – Go Live**: New process or tool in use, old process retired.
- **M6 – Review**: Project closed, lessons learned logged, final budget checked.

Milestones are recorded in the Project Status Notes with a target date and an actual date. If a milestone slips by more than two weeks, the lead must tell Helen and update the status notes the same day.

**12.5 Project Status Notes**

The Project Status Notes file is the single source of truth for project progress. It is a spreadsheet on the shared drive, with one tab per project. Each tab has columns for:

The internal memo records Project Atlas's project kickoff date as 2026-02-02. Record status: historical.

- Milestone number and name
- Target date (ISO format, YYYY-MM-DD)
- Actual date (left blank until the milestone is reached)
- Owner
- Notes (brief, no more than a couple of sentences)

The lead (or the deputy, if the lead is away) updates the status notes every Friday by 4pm. If there is nothing to update, the lead writes "No change" in the notes column for the most recent milestone rather than leaving it blank. This helps us see at a glance which projects are moving and which have stalled.

**12.6 Project Status Meetings**

We hold a project status meeting on the first Monday of each month, 10:00–11:00, in the meeting room on the first floor. The meeting is chaired by Helen. Each project lead gives a five-minute update covering:

- What has been completed since the last meeting.
- What is planned for the next month.
- Any risks or blockers, and who is helping to resolve them.

Notes from the meeting are taken by Amelia and circulated within two working days. Action items from the meeting are added to the Action Register (see section 13).

**12.7 Project Closures**

When a project reaches M6 and is ready to close, the lead must:

1. Confirm all milestones are marked complete in the status notes.
2. Log the lessons learned in the Lessons Learned file (one page maximum).
3. Confirm the final budget with Helen and flag any overspend.
4. Move the project folder on the shared drive to Projects / Closed / [Year] / [Project Name].

Once a project is closed, the Xero project code is archived. Do not reuse a closed project code for new work – ask Amelia if you need a new code.

If your return or payment is late, you may be liable to a surcharge. The
surcharge regime works as follows:

- First late submission: you will receive a warning letter and be placed in a

- Further late submissions within that period: surcharges are calculated on a
  sliding scale, starting at 2% of the VAT due, rising to 5%, 10%, or 15% for

| 7   | Total value of purchases and other expenses, excluding any VAT. Enter the total value of all purchases and expenses you have incurred in the period, including those on which you cannot reclaim VAT. Do not include any VAT. |
| 8   | Total value of all supplies of goods and related services to other EU countries. Enter the total value of goods you have dispatched to other EU countries and related services. This box is used for Intrastat purposes. |
| 9   | Total value of all acquisitions of goods and related services from other EU countries. Enter the total value of goods you have received from other EU countries and related services. |

**Example: first return**

Meadow & Thorne is a small floristry business that registered for VAT on
1 January 2026. Its first VAT period runs from 1 January 2026 to 31 March
2026. The quarter end date for this first return is 31 March 2026.

During the period, Meadow & Thorne made sales of £12,000 excluding VAT.
The VAT on these sales at 20% was £2,400. The business also bought new
display shelving for £1,500 excluding VAT, and the VAT on this was £300.
The business has no EU acquisitions or supplies.

The owner, Amelia, completes the return as follows:

The HMRC guidance states VAT Return Q1 2026's quarter end date is 2026-03-31. Record status: historical.

- Box 1: 2400
- Box 2: 0
- Box 3: 2400
- Box 4: 300
- Box 5: 2100 (this is the amount payable to HMRC)
- Box 6: 12000
- Box 7: 1500
- Box 8: 0
- Box 9: 0

The return is submitted online, and the £2,100 is paid by direct debit on
the deadline. Meadow & Thorne keeps a copy of the return and the VAT
invoices for the shelving and for its sales.

**Common mistakes to avoid**

When completing your return, please take care to avoid the following
common errors:

- Entering figures in the wrong box. Always double-check that the figure
  you have entered relates to the correct box, especially for boxes 6 to 9.
- Forgetting to include VAT on goods you have imported from outside the UK.
  This VAT is due in box 1, even though you may be able to reclaim it in
  box 4.
- Reclaiming input tax without a valid VAT invoice. You must hold a valid
  VAT invoice for any purchase on which you reclaim VAT. If you do not have
  an invoice, you cannot reclaim the VAT.
- Mixing up the total value of supplies (box 6) with the VAT on those
  supplies (box 1). Box 6 is always the value excluding VAT.
- Submitting a nil return when you have made no sales but have incurred
  expenses. You should still complete boxes 4, 7 and 9 where appropriate.

**Confirmation of VAT registration**

I am writing to confirm that Meadow & Thorne has been registered for Value Added Tax with effect from 1 January 2026. Your VAT registration number is shown above. Please quote this number on all correspondence and on any invoices you issue.

**What happens next**

You will receive your first VAT return for the period 1 January 2026 to 31 March 2026. This return will be issued to your Government Gateway account in early April. You should complete and submit this return by the deadline shown on the return itself.

If you have not received your return by 10 April 2026, please contact us using the details at the end of this letter. Do not wait until near the deadline before contacting us, as this may leave insufficient time to resolve any issue before the return is due.

**Paying VAT**

You can pay the VAT you owe in a number of ways. The quickest and easiest method is by Direct Debit. If you have not already set up a Direct Debit, you can do this through your Government Gateway account or by contacting your bank. Payments by Direct Debit are taken automatically on the day after the deadline, so you do not need to worry about missing a payment date.

Other payment methods include:

- Online or telephone banking (Faster Payments or CHAPS)
- Debit or credit card through the HMRC payment portal
- Bank transfer at your bank or building society
- At your Post Office (you will need a payment slip from HMRC)

Please note that if you pay by a method other than Direct Debit, you should allow sufficient time for the payment to reach HMRC. Payments made by Faster Payments usually arrive on the same day, but payments by other methods can take up to three working days. If your payment is late, you may be charged interest and a surcharge.

Please make sure you quote your payment reference (shown above) whenever you make a payment. This helps us apply the payment to your account quickly and accurately.

**Keeping records**

You are required to keep records of all sales and purchases for at least six years. These records must be sufficient to allow a complete and accurate VAT return to be prepared. You should keep:

- Copies of all VAT invoices you issue
- VAT invoices for all goods and services you buy
- Records of any goods you import or export
- A summary of the VAT you charge and the VAT you reclaim

You may keep these records in paper or electronic form, but you must be able to produce them to HMRC when asked.

**If you need help**

If you have any questions about this letter, your registration, or your VAT obligations, please visit the VAT section of our website or contact the VAT helpline. You will need your VAT registration number when you call.

Telephone: 0300 200 3700
Opening hours: 8am to 6pm, Monday to Friday

**Please keep this letter safe.** You may need to show it to your bank, your suppliers, or your accountant as proof of your VAT registration.

Yours sincerely

K. Okafor

HM Revenue & Customs
